sources.title: Michal Biran: Ilak-Khanids, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct scholarly article read. Origins debated; mid-late tenth century to early thirteenth century. Around 1040 division, 1089 Seljuk intervention, 1134 Balasaghun, 1141 Qatwan, eastern termination in 1211 and western/Ferghana termination in 1212-13. No claim of an exact 840 founding or uniform borders.

sources.title: Dilnoza Duturaeva: Qarakhanid Roads to China (Brill, 2022)
sources.note: Open-access scholarly monograph, full PDF hosted by Library of Congress; selected passages read directly. Printed p.16 royal clan and divided capitals; pp.67-70 delegation rules and Meng Yuanlao court account. Chinese source translation is paraphrased, not quoted. PDF page index equals printed page plus 22.

sources.title: Ancient Taraz Historical and Cultural Museum-Reserve: Settlement of Taraz
sources.note: Direct museum text read. Tenth-twelfth-century bathhouses; 1938 and 1960s excavations, wall decoration, clay seat, four rooms, and 2011-16 archaeology of residential/commercial buildings, water supply and caravanserais. Unrelated historical-name errors on the page are not adopted.

sources.title: Spengler, Maksudov and colleagues: Arboreal crops on the medieval Silk Road (2018)
sources.note: Direct primary paper read, abstract, methods, arboreal-crop discussion and Figure 4. Tashbulak ninth-eleventh centuries is explicitly earlier regional context. The 2018 correction, DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0204582, corrects only Frachetti’s institutional affiliation. Apple/pear ambiguities and orchard/wild distinctions not flattened.

sources.title: Frantz Grenet: Samarqand, history and archaeology
sources.note: Direct article by excavator read, especially Qarakhanid pavilions, 1066 waqf documents and southern suburbs. Do not attribute eighth-century chess/school finds to Qarakhanids. Madrasa precise archaeological identification remains disputed.

sources.title: Kyrgyz Republic nomination: Silk Roads Sites in Kyrgyzstan, Uzgen
sources.note: Direct national Tentative List submission hosted by UNESCO read. Uzgen mausoleums, inscriptions dated 1152, 1186 and 1187, terracotta/plaster, and four rectangular late-twelfth-century pottery furnaces 0.4 km north. This is not an inscription of Uzgen on the World Heritage List.

sources.title: World Bank/GFDRR: Uzbekistan resilient cultural heritage and sustainable tourism development (2020)
sources.note: Direct PDF, Annex III ministry technical assessment, printed p.40 / PDF index 55. Kalyan minaret, 1127 Arslan Khan, inscription names builder Bako; steep internal spiral staircase.

sources.title: Manuscript Institution of Türkiye: Dîvânu Lügati’t-Türk, second edition
sources.note: Institutional indexed original Turkish product description fully readable: written 1072-74 in Baghdad for teaching Turkic to Arabic speakers; only known manuscript copied 1 August 1266, Millet Library Ali Emiri Arabi 4189. English facsimile introduction p.98 independently indexed under PDF 8e7a33d5-2df2-461e-85d1-d93bad6d6ed2.pdf confirms chronology; broad dynasty date in that introduction not used.

sources.title: Ashmolean Museum, Heberden Coin Room: Qarakhanid copper coin, HCR14528
sources.note: Full indexed original record checked with exact query "HCR14528"; direct page fetch failed. Obverse Arabic and museum translation; reverse names Sulayman Tafghaj Khan; copper fals, unknown mint, before 574 AH / before 1178 CE, 30.5 mm. Museum purchased it in 1966, not a documented excavation. Arabic line breaks joined for excerpt; no palaeographic reconstruction.

proposedOverrides.name: Qarakhanids
proposedOverrides.summary: Central Asian Turkic dynasty with divided eastern and western realms.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Exact indexed spelling retained as ID; public conventional name Qarakhanids. No runtime card/override or duplicate indexed Qarakhanid label found. Broad polygon extends well south of the Amu Darya into areas that should not be treated as proven Qarakhanid territory; not silently corrected or validated. It also conflates separated eastern and western branches. Public overview warns oversized single outline and coverage dates. History, hospital endowments, Tashbulak and diplomatic scenes before 1100 are labelled earlier context; termination after 1200 explicitly later. Preserve coverage bounds rather than invent exact historical start. No other identities attached.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Contemporary dynasty coin uses Arabic; no claim that this is Turkic vernacular. Later manuscript copy is separately labelled.
